newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Mercator wins EBRD loan.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Mercator wins EBRD loan.

text.p: The European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Friday it had arranged a 140 million mark (75 million Ecu) financing package for Slovenian trading company Mercator.

The package, which was arranged jointly with the Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), will finance the construction of new supermarkets and hypermarkets and the refurbishment of around 100 existing stores.
"This is the largest EBRD project so far in the private sector in Slovenia," Olivier Descamps, Director of the EBRD's Slovenia Team said in a statement sent to Reuters.
The EBRD is providing 60 million marks, with six participating banks contributing the remaining 80 million.
The syndicate banks are UBS, Bayerische Vereinsbank, Dresdner Bank Luxembourg, Kredietbank, Creditanstalt and Societe Generale.

"The fact that the EBRD and UBS were able to syndicate a large portion of the loan reflects the quality of Mercator and the willingness of international banks to accept, for the first time, long-term exposure to private Slovenian companies," said Noreen Doyle, the EBRD's Deputy Vice President for Credit and Commercial Co-Financing.

The project is the 18th signed by the EBRD in Slovenia. So far EBRD investment in the country totals 338 million Ecu, equivalent to some 160 Ecu per capita, which is a higher EBRD per capita investment than in any other transition economy.
Mercator operates in domestic retail and wholesale markets, managing over 650 stores around Slovenia and a number of high quality food processing companies.
In 1995 Mercator had a net profit of 4.6 million marks up from 0.08 milllion in 1994, which, the company said, was a particularly tough year.
Turnover rose to 36.3 million marks in 1995 from 31.9 million.
Mercator is listed on the over-the-counter (OTC) market of the Ljubljana bourse. On Friday morning its share rose 1.04 percent to 3,980 tolars.
